name: Asymmetric text-dominant hero
description: A hero composition where typography carries most of the visual weight; a small abstract or diagrammatic element balances it rather than a photo.
when_to_use: No strong hero image/screenshot exists but the headline and positioning are strong.
constraints: Requires a confident, short headline; avoid when hero copy is long or hedging.

name: Split hero with abstract visual
description: A two-column hero: copy on one side, a generated abstract/geometric visual or diagram on the other, in place of a missing photo.
when_to_use: The profile has a strong narrative thesis but no real hero image to anchor the composition.
constraints: The abstract visual must represent an approved concept, never imply real evidence (e.g. a real screenshot).

name: Centered minimal hero
description: A single centered headline/subhead/CTA block with generous whitespace and no competing visual element.
when_to_use: Sparse profiles with limited content where restraint reads as confidence rather than emptiness.
constraints: Needs enough vertical rhythm/spacing discipline elsewhere on the page to avoid feeling incomplete.

name: Vertical career/experience timeline
description: A vertical rail with dated milestones branching left/right, used to narrate a career or project history in sequence.
when_to_use: A route needs to show progression over time across multiple roles or project phases.
constraints: Long labels need a condensed mobile treatment (single column, shorter dates) — do not keep the branching layout on narrow viewports.

name: Horizontal milestone strip
description: A short, horizontally scannable strip of 3-5 key milestones, used as a compact summary rather than a full history.
when_to_use: A brief 'at a glance' progression is useful but a full vertical timeline would be too heavy for the route's density.
constraints: Horizontal scroll/overflow on mobile needs an explicit fallback (e.g. collapse to a stacked list).

name: Before/after comparison diagram
description: A two-state diagram contrasting a prior state and an improved state (e.g. latency, process steps, architecture) to make an outcome legible without real screenshots.
when_to_use: A claim references a measurable or structural improvement but no chart/screenshot evidence exists.
constraints: Only label states that are grounded in approved claim_grounding — never fabricate specific numbers.

name: Process/flow diagram
description: A step-sequence diagram (boxes/arrows) illustrating a workflow, retry/backoff strategy, or pipeline stage progression.
when_to_use: A project's technical contribution is best explained as a sequence of decisions/steps rather than prose alone.
constraints: Keep step count low enough to remain legible in a single-column mobile layout; simplify rather than shrink text.

name: Abstract system-topology diagram
description: A generalized node-and-edge diagram representing an approved system structure, without claiming to be a real internal architecture document.
when_to_use: Illustrating system design depth for a backend/infrastructure-heavy profile with no real diagram available.
constraints: Must stay abstract/representative — never presented as a real internal document or exact production topology.

name: Case-study evidence grid
description: A grid of framed evidence tiles (screenshots, diagrams, or artifacts) supporting a project case study.
when_to_use: Multiple approved visual artifacts exist for one route and benefit from being seen together rather than one at a time.
constraints: Grid density must collapse to a single column on mobile; never crop a tile in a way that loses its focal point.

name: Single-focus framed evidence panel
description: One large, framed evidence visual with supporting caption, used when only one strong asset exists for a route.
when_to_use: Exactly one strong approved image/diagram exists for a route and deserves emphasis rather than dilution in a grid.
constraints: Requires a real focal point/safe-crop region if the asset is a photo; avoid forcing an aspect ratio the source can't support.

name: Generative abstract gradient-mesh background
description: A soft, low-contrast generative gradient or mesh texture used as a background layer, never as foreground content.
when_to_use: A scene needs visual depth/atmosphere but has no photographic asset and should not look flat.
constraints: Must stay low-contrast enough not to interfere with foreground text legibility; disable/simplify under reduced-motion.

name: Subtle grid/dot texture background
description: A faint structural grid or dot-matrix texture, reinforcing a technical/engineering visual personality without imagery.
when_to_use: The visual language leans technical/precise and benefits from a structural background motif.
constraints: Keep opacity low; texture must never compete with primary content for attention.

name: Sticky minimal top navigation
description: A slim, persistent top navigation bar with a small number of primary destinations plus a primary CTA.
when_to_use: A multi-page or hybrid site needs consistent cross-route orientation.
constraints: Must define an explicit mobile collapse strategy (e.g. condensed menu) before nav item count grows past a handful.

name: Single-page anchor nav with scroll progress
description: In-page anchor navigation (optionally with a scroll-progress indicator) for a single long page instead of route-based navigation.
when_to_use: The site is a single scrolling page with clearly delineated sections worth jumping between.
constraints: Anchor targets must map to real section_ids from Content Architect; never invent a section that doesn't exist.

name: Staged scroll-reveal entrance
description: Content within a scene fades/rises into place in a short staggered sequence as it enters the viewport.
when_to_use: A signature moment scene benefits from a controlled entrance without relying on a specific animation library.
constraints: Requires an explicit reduced-motion fallback (static, fully visible state) and must never gate critical content behind the animation.

name: Hover-lift micro-interaction for cards
description: A small elevation/scale shift on hover for card-like elements (project index, gallery tiles) to signal interactivity.
when_to_use: Card-based navigation elements (e.g. project index, gallery) need a lightweight interactive affordance.
constraints: Hover-only interactions need a touch-equivalent (e.g. visible affordance without hover) since touch devices have no hover state.

name: Line-weight technical/interface icon set
description: A consistent-stroke, line-based icon family for interface affordances (navigation, links, states) and simple technology/concept markers.
when_to_use: The visual language is restrained/technical and needs interface icons or lightweight concept markers without photographic or brand imagery.
constraints: Never substitute for a real technology/brand logo — use a generic line icon or text label when no approved logo exists.

name: Capability/skill-group badge icons
description: A small set of abstract badge-style marks used to visually distinguish grouped capability/skill categories from each other.
when_to_use: A dense skills/capability inventory needs a scannable visual anchor per group without turning into a decorative wall.
constraints: Badges are a grouping aid, not evidence — never imply certification, verification, or an external endorsement that was not supplied.

name: Editorial display + technical body pairing
description: A confident, restrained display face for headlines paired with a highly legible, slightly technical body/mono-adjacent face for explanatory and code-adjacent text.
when_to_use: The visual personality is calm, technical, and editorial rather than playful or marketing-driven.
constraints: Keep the display face restrained — avoid decorative or script faces that undercut a technical/credible tone.

name: Warm approachable display + body pairing
description: A slightly rounded, friendly display face paired with a warm, comfortable body face — for profiles whose positioning is approachable rather than austere.
when_to_use: The visual personality calls for warmth and approachability without sacrificing legibility or credibility.
constraints: Keep contrast and legibility strong even with rounder letterforms; avoid faces that read as informal to the point of undermining credibility.
